title: Care Academy Q&A: Earlier Delivery-Charge Refunds and the Late Delivery Refund
content:
**Rule.** On a Delivery Claims Late Delivery Claim, the repeat-refund share depends on the delivery-charge refunds already paid under delivery claims on the customer's orders: counting the order-level refunds with reason delivery claim and no order line (refunds of a delivery charge rather than of merchandise) dated in the trailing 12 calendar months, as they stand on the orders' payment records, two or more such refunds pay 50% of the basis, exactly one pays 75%, and none leaves the basis whole.

| Such refunds in the trailing 12 calendar months | Share of the basis paid |
|---|---|
| none | 100% — the basis whole |
| exactly 1 | 75% |
| 2 or more | 50% |

**Where are these refunds found?**
On the payment records of the customer's orders: each order-level refund shows its reason. The refunds counted are those whose reason is delivery claim and which name no order line.

**Does a merchandise refund made under a claim count?**
No. A merchandise refund is booked against an order line; only refunds with no order line — refunds of a delivery charge — are counted.

**Which orders are looked at?**
All of the customer's orders. A refund counts whichever of the customer's orders it was paid on.

**What period is covered?**
The 12 calendar months up to today, by the date of each refund entry. A refund dated 13 months ago is not counted.

**Do refunds for other reasons count — a return, a cancellation?**
No. Only refunds whose reason is delivery claim are counted.

**Hypothetical case.** In the last 12 months a customer has had two delivery-claim refunds: one of 6.95 USD with no order line and one of 48.00 USD booked against a coat line. Only the first is a delivery-charge refund, so the count is exactly 1 and the share paid is 75% of the basis.
